question: What journal entries does each party book in a tokenized trade?
answer: The entries follow the economic object, not the technology. At each step only the parties whose own books hold the cash, the security or the claim debit or credit anything; a token, a chain or a software provider books nothing by itself. The cards below print every entry, step by step.

sections.title: Step by step, with the books
sections.sub: If this entity’s proprietary books do not debit or credit the economic object, they are not the issuer, holder, CCP, cash settler or reserve owner. A fiduciary file can still be a real role. Transport, software and an unused issuer register have no entry.

routes.title: Buy a broker-held security
routes.intro: Worked example: Trade amount $10,000. Already-issued CNS-eligible cash equity. Cede is already the registered holder. Teaching amount $10,000.

steps.title: Open the account
steps.q: Does anyone book the security yet?
steps.test: An account relationship is not a securities entitlement.

entries.role: Future beneficial owner — not yet a holder
entries.note: Customer agreement only.
Customer master file. No security on the books.
Opening a brokerage account does not touch the issuer.

steps.title: Trade date — obligations, not delivery
steps.q: Who now owes the security and the money?
steps.test: Trade-date entries create intermediary claims. The issuer and nominee still have no entry.

entries.note: Asset is an entitlement against the broker, not registered title.
This payable is to the street, not yet proven to be a CCP member payable.
Inverse of the buyer.

entries.role: Not the holder, CCP or cash settler
entries.note: Matching is not clearing, depository settlement, or cash.

entries.role: Not the obligor of this secondary trade
entries.note: Secondary trade does not recapitalize the issuer.

entries.role: Nominee idle — register already names this office
entries.note: Teaching assumption: Cede is already the registered holder.

steps.title: Clear — CCP becomes the counterparty
steps.q: Who books receivables and payables as principal to both members?
steps.test: That principal pair is the CCP. The member who has the CCP receivable/payable is the clearing member. The firm who has the customer receivable/payable is the carrying broker. They can be one legal person or two — the entries say.

entries.note: Matching without NSCC principal receivables/payables is not clearing. Which member sits across from NSCC stays unnamed.
See the LST table on this step. The CNS table is muni preference, not the equity CCP census.
Goldman is the teaching contrast: listed equity through NSCC (LST) without the muni-CNS symbol.

entries.dr: Clearing-fund asset or cash at CCP (if posted)
entries.cr: Cash or due to CCP (if posted)
entries.note: Show only if resources are actually posted. An unfunded net is not this entry.

steps.title: Settle — securities file and cash banks
steps.q: Which file moved the security, and whose bank books paid the money?
steps.test: CSD fiduciary debit/credit of participant positions is securities settlement. Settling-bank reserve or money-account entries are the cash role. Issuer register idle = not transfer-agent work.

entries.note: Taught office is DTC. This is the participant file, not DTC’s own portfolio.

entries.role: Intermediary entitlement holder vs the CSD
entries.note: Customer security is typically off-balance if properly safekept.
Current public list: 47 DTC settling banks. Member must designate one. Search the list on this step.
Same current list as the buying side. NSS nets settling-bank balances across DTC and NSCC.

entries.role: Cash-settlement operator of the FMI money obligation
entries.note: Layered with DTC settlement-agent and NSS rows on this same step.
Register still names the nominee.

entries.role: Idle — this is not direct registration
entries.note: If this register debit/credit holders, the process would be direct registration.
Name on the issuer register does not move.

entries.dr: NSCC net money figures received for NSS
entries.cr: NSS instruction submitted against settling-bank Fed accounts
entries.role: Settlement agent — prepares the cash instruction; does not replace the settling bank
entries.note: DTC as agent is a different office from DTC as CSD.

entries.cr: Settling-bank reserve account (net-net credit) / FMI settlement accounts
entries.role: Cash-settlement operator of the net-net bank balances
entries.note: A chain confirmation is not this NSS credit.

entries.who: Example DTC participant (not this teaching broker)
entries.occupant: Hidden Road Partners CIV US LLC
entries.dr: Participant securities position (if this entity were the teaching member)
entries.cr: No inference that this trade used this account
entries.role: Sourced example of a crypto-affiliated DTC participant
entries.note: Example only. Leave the teaching carrying broker unnamed.

steps.title: Hold — three records of the same security
steps.q: On whose books does the $10,000 now live?
steps.test: Beneficial owner, intermediary customer, participant, and registered nominee are different holder tiers. They must not share one role.

entries.cr: Payable to broker closed (if cash already paid)
entries.note: Claim is against the intermediary, not the issuer.

entries.role: Customer intermediary / entitlement holder vs CSD
entries.note: Properly safekept customer securities are not the broker’s proprietary inventory.

entries.cr: No further change at this step
entries.note: Taught office is DTC.
Issuer equity accounts unchanged.

steps.title: Service, exit, or fail
steps.q: Who books a distribution, a sale, or a loss?
steps.test: A market-value loss is not automatically a compensation claim. Failure stays on the CCP/member/settling-bank waterfall unless a source moves it.

entries.dr: Retained earnings or payable to holders (if a cash dividend is declared)
entries.cr: Cash (when paid to the nominee / CSD)
entries.role: Issuer or paying agent — only if a distribution actually occurs
entries.note: Ordinary hold has no such entry. Do not invent a dividend.

entries.cr: Payable to performing member remains until closed
entries.note: Teaching fail case — not an observed event.

routes.title: Subscribe to a fund
routes.intro: Worked example: Subscription amount $1,000,000. Issuer-led subscription for fund shares. Cash received at the fund’s custodian bank. Teaching amount $1,000,000. Not the exchange-traded route.

steps.title: Admit — application only
steps.q: Has cash or capital been booked?
steps.test: An application is memo. No million yet.

entries.occupant: BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund Ltd.
entries.note: Eligibility decision is not a capital credit.
No proprietary $1,000,000.

entries.role: Not the subscriber and not the cash bank
entries.note: Why issuer and manager cannot share one lane.
Application only at this step. No million on these books.

steps.title: Funding confirmed
steps.q: Who credited cash, and to whom is that cash a liability?
steps.test: The fund issuer credits capital. The custodian bank books a deposit owed to the fund. The IM still has no million. The TA still has no million.

entries.occupant: The Bank of New York Mellon
entries.role: Custodian as cash bank — liability to the fund
entries.note: Fund cash is usually this bank’s deposit obligation, not a token.

entries.occupant: BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund Ltd.
entries.note: Whoever credits capital is the issuer. The parent brand is not this entry.
Portfolio trades come later, as the fund’s entries, not the IM’s proprietary cash.

steps.title: Issue and record the holder
steps.q: Which credit is the share, and which file is the register?
steps.test: TA fiduciary credit of the holder is the issuer register. A token is the same share only if that register is the credit that moved. A second liability is a different claim.

entries.role: Holder of fund shares — not of each portfolio asset

entries.occupant: BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund Ltd.
entries.dr: — (cash already at B2, or reclass subscriptions to shares)

entries.note: Not a CSD participant file. Different office from Process A.

entries.occupant: The Bank of New York Mellon
entries.cr: Shareholder records aligned to the TA register
entries.role: Administrator — fiduciary books of the fund, not proprietary IM cash
entries.note: Same brand as custodian; two offices.

steps.title: Transfer to an eligible holder
steps.q: Did the register turn, or only a wallet?
steps.test: Holder-to-holder transfer: TA fiduciary debit/credit. Fund has no cash entry. Paying bank has no entry. Wallet-only movement without the register is not this role.

entries.note: Only if issue terms allow the transfer.

entries.occupant: BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund Ltd.
The Bank of New York Mellon

steps.title: Redeem and pay
steps.q: Did the custodian bank credit the investor, or only a token burn?
steps.test: Inverse of funding: fund Dr shares Cr cash; custodian bank Dr fund deposit Cr reserves. Burn without that bank credit has not paid the investor.

entries.occupant: BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund Ltd.
The Bank of New York Mellon

routes.title: Make a dollar payment
routes.intro: Worked example: Payment amount $1,000,000. Fedwire Funds payment, $1,000,000. Payer at Bank A, beneficiary at Bank B. USDC is a comparison process, not a Fedwire stage.

steps.title: Identify the claim
steps.q: What does the payer hold, and who owes it?
steps.test: A bank deposit is the customer’s asset and the bank’s liability. That is a different claim from USDC.

entries.role: Holder of a bank-deposit claim — opening position, no new entry
entries.note: The invoice being paid is a separate commercial claim.

entries.occupant: Payward Financial, Inc. d/b/a Kraken Financial
entries.role: Obligor of the payer’s money — opening position, no new entry
entries.note: Memo: no new entry at this step.

steps.title: Authorize and accept the order
steps.q: Is this recognition or only a message?
steps.test: Accepted payment order is still memo until funded and processed. A wallet signature is not Bank A’s debit.

entries.note: Authorization is not payment.

entries.occupant: Payward Financial, Inc. d/b/a Kraken Financial
entries.note: Example occupant only. The teaching payer’s bank remains unidentified.

entries.role: Service operator — not yet rebooking reserves
entries.note: Taught office is the Federal Reserve Banks.

steps.title: Provide sending-bank resources
steps.q: Did the sending bank have spendable funds, or only a message?
steps.test: A payment message does not supply reserves. Prefunding, overdraft and available balance are different entries.

entries.occupant: Payward Financial, Inc. d/b/a Kraken Financial
entries.dr: — (or Dr due from customer if not already collected)
entries.cr: Reserve or available settlement balance remains until C4
entries.note: Even this example does not prove funded use. Unlimited credit is expressly not granted.

steps.title: Complete the service transfer
steps.q: Whose liabilities to the two banks just rebooked?
steps.test: Fedwire always moves sending bank, Reserve Banks, and receiving bank. A USDC holder-to-holder transfer need not touch any of those books.

entries.occupant: Payward Financial, Inc. d/b/a Kraken Financial
entries.role: Sending participant / obligor of the payer’s money
entries.note: If this entity were Bank A, its reserve account would move. It is not asserted to be Bank A here.
They rebook their own liabilities to the two banks. Fedwire-as-message is not a fourth $1,000,000 claim.

entries.role: Receiving participant / new obligor to the beneficiary
entries.note: Teaching receiving bank unnamed. A USDC recipient bank is a different seat on redemption payout.
If it only coordinates a commitment, it has no $1,000,000 proprietary entry. See the saved SWIFT Saturday walkthrough.

steps.title: What the recipient received
steps.q: Which bank now owes the beneficiary, and is the invoice a separate entry?
steps.test: Receiving bank’s customer-deposit credit is the money the beneficiary holds. Discharge of the payer’s invoice is a commercial entry on payer/beneficiary books, not the Fedwire rule.

entries.role: Holder of the new deposit claim

entries.note: Article 4-A-style teaching: acceptance creates the duty to pay the beneficiary.

steps.title: Exception, return, or redeem
steps.q: Is this an error on Process C, or a different asset exiting to dollars?
steps.test: Fedwire exception stays on bank/Fed books. USDC redemption is inverse of mint, then Process C for the dollar payout. Burn without that bank credit is not payout.

entries.dr: Correction / receivable as the rule provides
entries.cr: Customer deposit or reserve as the rule provides
entries.role: Exception handler under the transfer rules
entries.note: Teaching placeholder — not a named fail.

uncertain: Illustrative teaching entries for role discrimination. Not GAAP or IFRS policy and not a named firm’s actual journal. Named occupants are sourced legal persons or process offices for that seat. Unnamed seats are evidence gaps, not empty markets. A brand, parent, token or chain does not inherit the seat.
These are illustrative entries for working out who plays which role, not any named firm's actual books.

catalog_context.title: Accounting built from shared business events
catalog_context.answer: Accounting is moving from piecing together scattered records after the fact to building the books from shared business events. Licenses, accounting labels, audit reports and corrections are also being used to decide who may act, invest or rely on the result.

catalog_context.title: Who actually controls the crypto infrastructure
catalog_context.answer: Of 20 crypto networks and companies we track, only one is used at scale and none is proven under stress; many brands rest on a handful of legal providers.
